newsitem.title: USA: U.S. March production surges, strains factory use rates.
newsitem.headline: U.S. March production surges, strains factory use rates.

text.p: A steep surge in industrial output during March drove the nation's mines, factories and utilities to their highest operating rates in two years, the Federal Reserve said on Wednesday.
Production climbed an unexpectedly strong 0.9 percent last month after a revised 0.6 percent February pickup as a manufacturing boom continued in March.

The capacity use rate, which measures how near to production limits that businesses are operating at, jumped to 84.1 percent from a revised 83.6 percent in February. It was the highest rate since 84.3 percent in March 1995 and may raise a red flag on potential inflation by increasing fears of higher wage and price demands.

"Demand is vigorous, shelves are empty, and this will continue to push existing capacity pressure," said economist Kevin Flanagan of Dean Witter Reynolds Inc. in New York. "This will definitely capture the Fed's attention."

The U.S. central bank increased short-term interest rates by a quarter percentage point late last month, seeking to cool demand and to sustain the economy's expansion by preventing inflationary pressures from building.

Financial markets reacted almost immediately to the output report as prices fell on the New York Stock Exchange and long-term bond yields climbed sharply on revived concerns that the Fed may raise rates further to combat inflation.

The Fed said that U.S. industrial output climbed at an annual rate of 5.6 percent in the first quarter this year, up from 4.5 percent in the final three months of last year, when strikes in the auto industry put a damper on output.
Total manufacturing production jumped by 0.9 percent in both February and March this year, driven by gains in output of costly and long-lasting durable goods like household appliances and computers.
Production by mining industries was up 0.9 percent in March after a strong 1.5 percent gain in February.
Utilities companies boosted their output by 0.8 percent last month following a 3.4 percent decline in February, when mild weather reduced electricity demand.
